'''Marie A. Vitulli''' is an American [[mathematician]] and professor emerita at the [[University of Oregon]].

==Mathematics==

Vitulli's research is in [[commutative algebra]] and applications to [[algebraic geometry]]. More specific topics in her research include [[deformation theory|deformations]] of monomial curves, [[seminormal ring]]s, the weak normality of commutative rings and algebraic varieties, weak subintegrality, and the theory of [[Valuation (algebra)|valuations]] for commutative rings.<ref name="falconer"/> Along with her colleague [[David Kent Harrison|David K. Harrison]], she developed a unified valuation theory for rings with zero divisors that generalized both Krull and Archimedean valuations.{{r|vvaln}}

She was an undergraduate at the [[University of Rochester]]<ref name="falconer"/> and
obtained her PhD in 1976 at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] under the supervision of Dock-Sang Rim. Her dissertation was ''Weierstrass Points and Monomial Curves''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=23130}}</ref>  The title of her 2014 Falconer lecture was "From Algebraic to Weak Subintegral Extensions in Algebra and Geometry."<ref name="csws">{{cite web|title=Marie A. Vitulli named 2014 AWM-MAA Falconer Lecturer|url=https://csws.uoregon.edu/share/news/may-20-2014/marie-vitulli-named-2014-awm-maa-falconer-lecturer |website=Center for the Study of Women in Society|publisher=University of Oregon|access-date=2023-04-11}}</ref>

==Activism==

Vitulli and political scientist [[Gordon Lafer]] led an effort to unionize faculty at the University of Oregon beginning in the spring of 2007.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Baez|first1=David|title=Labor Pains|url=https://www.eugeneweekly.com/2012/10/11/labor-pains/|website=Eugene Weekly|date=October 11, 2012 |access-date=7 March 2018}}</ref>  This effort eventually led to the formation of the United Academics at the University of Oregon.<ref>{{cite web|title=Our History|url=http://uauoregon.org/about/our-history/|website=United Academics of the University of Oregon|access-date=March 7, 2018|archive-date=June 18, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200618225928/http://uauoregon.org/about/our-history/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Vitulli heads the Women in Math Project at the University of Oregon.<ref name="falconer"/><ref>{{citation|url=https://pages.uoregon.edu/wmnmath/|title=The Women in Math Project|publisher=University of Oregon|access-date=2018-03-09}}</ref>
With [[Mary Flahive]], Vitulli has also studied patterns in hiring among women mathematicians.<ref>{{citation|title=Complexities: Women in Mathematics|title-link= Complexities: Women in Mathematics |first1=Bettye Anne|last1=Case|author1-link=Bettye Anne Case|first2=Anne M.|last2=Leggett|author2-link=Anne M. Leggett|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=2016|isbn=9781400880164|at=[https://books.google.com/books?id=PNIJDAAAQBAJ&pg=PA107 p. 107]}}</ref> Vitulli has also written about the difficulties involved with documenting the lives of female mathematicians on Wikipedia.<ref>
{{cite arXiv |last=Vitulli |first=Marie A. |eprint=1710.11103 |title=Writing Women in Mathematics into Wikipedia |class=math.HO |date=2017 }}</ref>

Vitulli participated in the panel discussion held as the first official activity of [[Spectra (mathematical association)|Spectra]] at the 2015 [[Joint Mathematics Meetings]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bryant |first1=Robert |last2=Buckmire |first2=Ron |last3=Khadjavi |first3=Lily |last4=Lind |first4=Doug |title=The Origins of Spectra, an Organization for LGBT Mathematicians |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |date=June–July 2019 |volume=66 |issue=6 |pages=875–882 |doi=10.1090/noti1890 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201906/rnoti-p875.pdf|doi-access=free }}</ref> She endowed the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] Marie A. Vitulli Graduate Fellowship to "support one advanced graduate student in mathematics, per academic year, to attend an MSRI program with their advisor."<ref>{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=https://www.msri.org/|access-date=2022-01-04|website=www.msri.org}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Vitulli was recognized as an [[AWM/MAA Falconer Lecturer]] in 2014.<ref name="falconer">{{cite web|title=Marie A. Vitulli|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/falconer-lectures/falconer-lecture-2014/|work=Past Falconer Lecturers|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|access-date=7 March 2018}}</ref>  Vitulli received a Service Award from the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=AWM service award 2017 |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-service-award/awm-service-award-2017/ |access-date= |website=Association for Women in Mathematics}}</ref>

She is part of the 2019 class of fellows of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2019-awm-fellows/|title=2019 Class of AWM Fellows|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|access-date=2018-10-07}}</ref>
She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2020 Class, for "contributions to commutative algebra, and for service to the mathematical community particularly in support of women in mathematics".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2020 |access-date=2022-05-04 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>
